scoring._README: score = sum of the components below. Higher = more brief-worthy. Candidates are pre-sorted by score desc; each item's `score_breakdown` shows its parts.
scoring.recency: 0–1h = 2.3 (breaking) · 1–3h = 2.0 (fresh) · then linear decay to 0 by 24h · unknown = 0.5
scoring.signal: AI/tech (or watchlist) keyword hits — match_count capped at 5 × 0.6
scoring.source: outlet authority from trusted-sources.md: primary (company/lab) 2.0 · citation 1.2 · screening 0.5 · other 1.0
scoring.corrob: cross-outlet corroboration — how many outlets ran the same headline (cluster_size − 1, capped 3) × 0.8
scoring.watchlist: watchlist stream only: matched company tier — Tier-1 +1.5 · Tier-2 +0.8

candidates.title: Oracle and Wild Bio Join Forces to Advance AI-Driven Agriculture
candidates.description: Oracle and Wild Bio Join Forces to Advance AI-Driven Agriculture    Oracle
candidates.body_text: Oracle News Press Release Oracle and Wild Bio Join Forces to Advance AI-Driven Agriculture Collaboration will help advance AI-powered research for more productive, resilient crops and scalable, high-quality carbon removal Austin, Texas, and Oxford, United Kingdom—24 September 2026 Oracle and Wild Bioscience (Wild Bio) today announced a collaboration to advance agricultural resilience and crop-based carbon removal using AI. As part of the partnership, Wild Bio plans to use Oracle Cloud and Oracle IoT technology to support its field research. Wild Bio is using AI to tackle two major challenges in agriculture: maintaining crop productivity as environmental stress increases and developing crop varieties that can remove more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Both efforts build on the same idea—AI can learn from millions of years of plant evolution and identify traits that can improve how crops perform. “AI is creating new opportunities to solve problems that once seemed out of reach,” said Clay Magouyrk, chief executive officer, Oracle. “Wild Bio is a powerful example of how combining AI with deep scientific expertise can turn new ideas into practical solutions with the potential to improve lives around the world.” Wild Bio’s platform uses AI to analyze plant genomes and identify genetic traits that have helped wild plants adapt and thrive over time. NEW YORK, Sept 24 : Oracle's move to protect itself against potential delays at a massive data center project developed by Blue Owl in New Mexico sent a chill through the trillion-dollar market for AI infrastructure financing, according to interviews with bankers and investors. Oracle issued a force majeure notice in connection with Jupiter, a data center campus Blue Owl unit STACK Infrastructure is building to support OpenAI, the latest setback for a sector where lenders and investors are growing more cautious about financing the industry's breakneck expansion. Blue Owl said the notice did not alter the parties' commitment to the project. Even so, the event is reverberating through discussions around other proposed data center financings, including SB Energy, which is developing a campus to serve OpenAI in Ohio, a person close to its financing said. candidates.title: Google is sending a teensy-tiny AI data center to space
candidates.description: It's an experiment to see how the chips hold up in the harsh vacuum of the cosmos.
candidates.body_text: It's an experiment to see how the chips hold up in the harsh vacuum of the cosmos. Google Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Google's Project Suncatcher, which ultimately aims to put large AI installations in low-Earth orbit , is preparing for a milestone event. The company will be sending a teensy-tiny AI data center into space to see how it reacts to the harsh conditions, as reported by The New York Times . A satellite named MVP will be aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket set to launch on October 1, where it will be placed into orbit. This isn't a full data center in the conventional sense. It's four specialized computer chips called "tensor processing units" which, combined, offer the power of a single server in a data center. We're taking AI to space with @Google . 🛰️ Project Suncatcher explores putting AI compute in orbit, powered by the sun. Soon, we'll be sending our first satellite into space to start testing that idea. It's a new approach to AI infrastructure. Check out a behind-the-scenes look... pic.twitter.com/cup8uXuyrC — Planet (@planet) September 24, 2026 Solar panels will supply just one kilowatt of power to juice the chips, which is equivalent to the energy needed to run a hair dryer. Google says this will be enough to test the hardware against the harsh conditions of space.
